subject: Nanotechnology
title: Photodynamic Therapy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Photodynamic Therapy usable.

hook.text: Load a nanoparticle with a photosensitizer, shine light, and it generates toxic oxygen that kills cancer cells.

buildup.text: Photosensitizers absorb light and transfer energy to oxygen — creating singlet oxygen, a potent cell killer.

discovery.text: Nanoparticles protect the photosensitizer from degradation and deliver it selectively to tumor tissue.

twist.text: Tumors are often hypoxic — low oxygen limits singlet oxygen production exactly where you need it most.

climax.text: Researchers design nano carriers that generate oxygen in situ or use type I reactions that need less oxygen.

punchline.text: Light plus oxygen plus nano equals targeted cell death.

quiz.question: What kills cancer cells in photodynamic therapy?
options: The nanoparticle itself dissolves the tumor
Singlet oxygen generated when a photosensitizer absorbs light
Heat from the absorbed light burns the cells
